steps.say: Liver hydatid disease starts with dog tapeworm eggs swallowed from contaminated soil or food. The embryos hatch in the gut and are carried most often to the right lobe of the liver. Seven in ten hydatid cysts are found in the liver, and they enlarge slowly, about a centimetre a year. Sheep rearing belts carry the heaviest burden.
steps.tx: **Echinococcus granulosus** (dog tapeworm from faecal contamination) forms **unilocular cyst** (single-fluid-chamber liver cysts) in **70** percent of hydatid cases, favouring the right lobe with growth of **1** cm per year. Pastoral sheep-rearing regions carry the highest burden, and liver screening follows lung imaging.

rows: Liver in 70 percent, right lobe favoured

steps.say: Not every hydatid cyst needs the same treatment, and the WHO ultrasound stages decide. Active fluid filled cysts are treated differently from dying transitional ones, while fully calcified dead cysts are simply watched. The wall sign on ultrasound is enough to stage most cysts without further scans. Matching treatment to stage avoids both overtreatment and recurrence.
steps.tx: **WHO staging** (ultrasound-based CE1 to CE5 activity scale) separates active unilocular and daughter-filled cysts from dying transitional forms and inactive **calcified cyst** (dead walled-off lesions with eggshell rims), deciding between drugs, PAIR and surgery. The detached laminated wall floating inside the cyst marks transitional stages on ultrasound, while solid heterogeneous contents signal degeneration.

steps.say: PAIR is the treatment for suitable cysts through the skin without open surgery. The cyst is punctured, its fluid drawn off, salty or alcohol solution is injected to kill the germinal layer, and everything is sucked back out. It is suited to larger active cysts past five centimetres. Bile connections must be ruled out first, because scolicidal fluid destroys bile ducts.
steps.tx: **PAIR** (puncture-aspiration-injection-reaspiration through the skin under ultrasound guidance) suits larger CE1 and CE3a cysts past **5** cm, killing the germ layer with hypertonic saline or alcohol **scolicidal** (sterilising fluid bath) with albendazole cover before and after. Hidden cyst-bile communication is excluded with contrast or MRCP beforehand, since scolicidal leaking into ducts causes stricturing cholangitis.

nodes.label: CE1 or CE3a cyst over 5 cm

steps.say: Albendazole is the drug backbone of every hydatid plan, before procedures, after them, or alone for small cysts. The classic schedule is 400 mg twice a day for 28 day cycles with fortnight breaks, though continuous courses are used with monitoring. Blood counts and liver enzymes are checked every cycle, because marrow suppression and hepatitis are the dreaded toxicities.
steps.tx: **Albendazole** (worm-killing tablets) **400** mg twice daily in **28-day cycles** (four weeks on drug) with **14**-day breaks sterilises small cysts and must precede and follow any intervention. Continuous courses need blood and liver monitoring, since marrow suppression and hepatitis complicate therapy.

vis.alt: Albendazole sulfoxide blocking tubulin polymerization and glucose uptake in worms.
vis.caption: Albendazole starves the germinal layer before and after any procedure. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Yellow skin with fever in a hydatid patient means the cyst has broken into the bile ducts. Fragments and daughter cysts wash down and block drainage, causing cholangitis. The blockage is cleared endoscopically first, then surgery closes the leak between cyst and duct and packs the cavity with omentum. Large connections sometimes need a new drainage join.
steps.tx: **Cystobiliary communication** (cyst ruptured into the bile ducts) declares itself with jaundice, cholangitis or hydatid membranes seen draining in bile, and needs ERCP clearance first plus surgery with cavity-bile leak closure and **omentoplasty** (omental packing that fills the residual cavity). Wide fistulae that will not seal may need biliary-enteric diversion instead of simple closure.

steps.say: The choice of operation depends on where the cyst sits. Cysts at the liver edge come out whole with their fibrous shells, which gives the lowest recurrence. Deep cysts hugging big vessels cannot be taken whole, so the roof is removed and the cavity stitched closed from within. Multiple or wrecked lobes need formal liver resection.
steps.tx: Edge-sited cysts allow **pericystectomy** (whole-capsule removal with a liver rim), while cysts hugging great vessels need partial removal with **capitonnage** (obliterating the cavity with sutures) to avoid catastrophic bleeding. Multiple or wrecked lobes need formal hepatic resection instead of repeated drainage attempts.

steps.say: Spilling live hydatid fluid into the belly is the catastrophe every precaution aims to prevent. The patient can collapse with anaphylaxis on the table, and every spilled protoscolex seeds a new cyst years later. Scolicidal soaked packs wall off the field, aspiration stays closed, and albendazole cover runs throughout. Adrenaline must be drawn up before the cyst is touched.
steps.tx: Spilling live cyst contents at operation means **spillage** (protoscolex-rich fluid escaping into the peritoneum), which risks **anaphylaxis** (mast-cell collapse with shock) and seeds secondary peritoneal hydatidosis years later. Scolicidal-soaked packs, closed aspiration and albendazole prophylaxis prevent both, and adrenaline readiness is mandatory before any cyst is opened.

vis.alt: Illustration of mast cell degranulation causing laryngeal oedema, bronchospasm and shock.
vis.caption: Spilled hydatid fluid triggers mast-cell anaphylaxis on the table. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The fox tapeworm causes a different and deadlier disease that behaves like liver cancer. It infiltrates across tissue planes rather than forming a neat cyst, so small operations always fail. Cure needs a cancer style resection with two centimetre clear margins plus two full years of albendazole. Disease strangling the hilum is considered for transplantation.
steps.tx: **Alveolar echinococcosis** (infiltrative fox-tapeworm liver disease) from **Echinococcus multilocularis** (tumour-like parasitic invasion across tissue planes) needs cancer-style radical resection with **2** cm clear margins plus **2** years of albendazole afterwards. Hilar disease that cannot be resected is considered for liver transplantation, since palliative debulking never cures this parasite.
